text: Find a comfortable position and let your body be still.
You do not need to go anywhere.
The journey we are about to take happens entirely within.
Breathe in and out. Again, breathe in and let everything fall away as you breathe out.
Let your shoulders drop, let your jaw unclench.
Feel the weight of your body against whatever holds you.
Now move your attention slowly downward.
The way you might pour something.
Forehead, eyes, throat, chest, belly, legs, feet.
Wherever you find holding, breathe into it and let it soften as you breathe out.
There is nowhere to be but here.
There is nothing to do but breathe.
Breathe in and out.
With each breath, let yourself become a little heavier,
a little more still.
Now, in your mind's eye, see yourself standing on desert sand at dusk.
Before you rises a mountain of stone, the great pyramid.
It is larger than you imagined and it is alive.
The teachers say the stones are alive, though few have understood this.
Feel it as you approach, a faint hum in the air, a pressure of presence,
as if the whole structure were breathing very slowly.
This place was built for one purpose that a person might need themselves.
Long ago, those who were ready would come here to be initiated,
to die to the small self and be reborn into a larger one.
You are going to walk that path now, in meditation, the way they walked it in body.
Walk toward the entrance, the passage is narrow and slopes downward.
Duck your head, the air grows cooler with every step.
The sounds of the desert fall away behind you,
the wind, the birds, the distant voices,
until there is only the sound of your own breathing and the soft scrape of your feet on stone.
Breathe in and out. Let the darkness gather around you like a blanket.
You come to a chamber, low and close.
This is the resonating chamber, the place of burial and resurrection.
Lie down here in your mind on the cool stone.
Feel how small the space is.
There is no way out except the way you came and you are not going back.
Let that land, for this little while, you are buried.
Notice what rises in you.
The mind does not like this.
It reaches for the exit, for light, for distraction.
Let it reach.
You do not have to follow.
This is the confrontation the chamber was built for.
The archetypal fear of being buried alive met not with escape but with stillness.
Breathe in and out.
Slower now.
As your senses withdraw, no sight, no sound, but breath, no movement,
something begins to loosen.
The desires you carry every day, the small hungers, the rehearsals of tomorrow,
watch them thin out like mist in morning sun.
This is the dying the teacher's speak of.
Not the death of the body, the death of the self that thought it was only a body.
And in the space that opens, something else arrives.
A sense of essential gain where there seemed only loss.
You are not less.
You are more.
More than the name you answer to.
More than the story you tell about yourself.
One meets the self, the guide say, in the center, in the deeps of the being.
You are in the deeps now.
Notice the quality of this new self.
It does not strive.
It does not defend.
It watches the old fears the way you might watch weather from a window.
There, real, but not you.
This is the transmutation the chamber was built to accomplish.
The same person minus the illusion of separateness.
Nothing was added.
Something false was removed.
Rest here a while.
Breathe in and out.
Let the stone hold you.
Let the dark do its work.
There is no hurry.
Initiation cannot be rushed.
It can only be allowed.
When you are ready, rise.
Not with your body, but with your attention.
And ascend to the king's chamber.
The passage climbs.
The air changes.
And here, in this high room of granite, the light is different.
Not the light of the sun, but a purified, centralized light,
intensified by the very shape of the stone around you.
Stand in the center of it.
This is the position of healing.
Feel the light moving through you, the way water moves through a sieve.
And feel what it carries away.
The distortions, the knots, the old tensions you have carried without knowing, let them leave.
You do not have to name them.
The light knows its work.
Breathe in and receive.
Breathe out and release.
Now, widen your attention.
The healing does not stop at your skin.
The teachers built this place so that initiates, once purified, could become channels,
carriers of this light outward.
And they built not one pyramid, but many.
Set like charged stones in a ring around the earth.
Each one balancing the incoming energy of creation against the distortions of the world.
You are sitting in your mind at one node of a planetary circuit,
so let it move through you to those you love.
Picture them, one by one, and let the light touch them.
Then wider, your city, your land, then widest, the whole planet,
turning blue and quiet beneath you,
receiving what you are giving without effort.
Feel the other nodes of the ring answering,
distant pyramids, distant chambers, the whole network coming with the same quiet current.
You are not doing this.
You are allowing it.
The light does the work.
You are the window it passes through.
A window does not strive to be transparent.
It only needs to be clean and to face the sun.
Breathe in and out.
Rest in the giving.
And now, gently, it is time to return.
The chamber dims.
The passages you climbed descend again in your mind.
You walk back out through the narrow corridor, ducking your head,
and step into the dusk air.
The desert is cool.
The stars are coming out, one by one.
In ratios, the old ones mapped with reverence.
You are not the same as when you entered.
Something was buried in there and something else walked out.
That is the whole of initiation.
And it is available to you every time you sit in stillness and consent to meet yourself.
Bring your attention back to your body now.
Feel its weight again.
Feel the surface beneath you.
The air on your skin.
Wiggle your fingers, your toes.
Take one deep breath in and let it out slowly.
Let the meditation end the way the initiation ends.
Not with the door slamming but with a quiet carrying forward.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
Walk gently and slowly back into your day.
Carrying quietly, what the pyramid was built to give.
The knowledge that the stones are alive and so are you.
And the light you met in the dark goes with you.
It was never about the stone.
It was always about the meeting.
